documents.title: Pin the agent to an explicit file list for scoped refactors
documents.body: Before a rename or signature change, list the exact files the agent may edit and tell it to stop and ask if another file needs a change. With the list in the prompt, my rename of a helper function touched only the three files I named instead of twenty call sites across the repo.
Worked for me. I renamed a function in two modules and gave the agent only those two paths. It asked before touching a third file instead of editing it silently.

documents.title: Let the agent run a repo-wide rename with the language server
documents.body: For a large rename, ask the agent to use the language server's rename action so every reference across the repository is updated in one pass, then review the full diff.
The LSP rename updated 48 references correctly, but it also renamed a string in a migration, so check the diff.

documents.title: Ask for a minimal diff and forbid drive-by formatting
documents.body: Agents often reformat whole files when they change one line, which hides the real change in review. Say: change only the lines required, do not reformat, reorder imports or fix unrelated style. Reject diffs that include untouched code.
Adding 'no drive-by formatting or whitespace changes outside the edited function' cut my review diffs from hundreds of lines to about twenty.

documents.title: Run the formatter in a pre-commit hook
documents.body: Install a pre-commit hook that runs the project formatter on staged files so every commit is formatted consistently, whether a person or an agent wrote it.

documents.title: Scope a schema change to one new migration file
documents.body: When adding a column, tell the agent to create exactly one new migration and never edit existing migrations, which may already have run in other environments. Ask it to update only the schema module and the changeset for that column.

documents.title: Squash old migrations before a major release
documents.body: After many releases, collapse historic migrations into a single structure dump to speed up test database setup. Do this only when every environment is current.

documents.title: Give each git worktree its own Postgres database
documents.body: Running two agents in two worktrees against one database makes their tests collide. Add a suffix from an environment variable to the database name in config, for example tips_dev_team2, and create it once per worktree. Each checkout then migrates and tests in isolation.
Used a DB suffix variable per worktree and parallel agent test runs stopped deadlocking on the same schema. Remember to drop the databases when you remove the worktree.

documents.title: Share one Docker Postgres container across all your projects
documents.body: Instead of installing Postgres per project, run a single container on a fixed port and point every project at it. Saves memory on a laptop.
One shared container works, but mind the max_connections setting once several apps have pools open.

documents.title: Load your login shell PATH for agents started outside a terminal
documents.body: Agents launched from an editor or a background service run a non-interactive shell that never reads your profile, so version managers like asdf or mise are missing and commands such as mix or node are not found. Start the agent from a login shell or export PATH explicitly in its environment.
This was it. The agent reported 'mix: command not found' until I added the mise shims directory to PATH in the launcher script.

documents.title: Pin tool versions with a .tool-versions file
documents.body: Commit a .tool-versions file so every developer and CI runner uses the same Elixir, Erlang and Node versions.

documents.title: Keep API keys in an owner-only file, never in the prompt
documents.body: Store provider keys in a file with mode 600 outside the repository and let the application read them. Never paste a key into the agent chat, because transcripts and logs are kept.

documents.title: Rotate a token immediately after it leaks into a log
documents.body: If a credential appears in CI output or a shared transcript, revoke and rotate it first, then clean up the logs.
Rotation took five minutes; finding every copy of the leaked log took a day.

documents.title: Ask for the first failing assertion, not a summary of all output
documents.body: When a large test suite fails, ask the agent to find the first failing test and quote its assertion message. Summaries of the whole run blur cause and effect.

documents.title: Redirect long command output to a file and let the agent grep it
documents.body: Instead of streaming a long build into the conversation, have the agent run the command with output redirected to a file, then search the file for errors. This keeps the context window for reasoning instead of log lines.

documents.title: Fix bcrypt_elixir compile failures on macOS by installing the command line tools
documents.body: If mix deps.compile fails with could not compile dependency :bcrypt_elixir, the C compiler is usually missing. Run xcode-select --install, then mix deps.clean bcrypt_elixir and compile again.
Exact same error after a macOS upgrade: `could not compile dependency :bcrypt_elixir, "mix compile" failed`. Reinstalling the command line tools fixed it.

documents.title: argon2_elixir NIF build fails on Alpine images
documents.body: On Alpine-based Docker images, install build-base before compiling argon2_elixir, otherwise the NIF build stops with make: not found.
Also needed erlang-dev on Alpine 3.20 for the NIF headers.

documents.title: Strip ANSI color codes before pasting logs
documents.body: Colored terminal output adds escape sequences that waste tokens and confuse agents. Pipe output through a filter that removes ANSI codes, or disable color with NO_COLOR=1.

documents.title: Use git worktrees to run two agents in parallel
documents.body: Create one worktree per task so two agents never edit the same checkout. Each worktree has its own branch and working directory.

documents.title: Fix DBConnection queue timeouts in tests
documents.body: The error (DBConnection.ConnectionError) connection not available and request was dropped from queue after 2000ms usually means async tests hold more connections than the pool allows. Raise pool_size for the test repo or find the test that checks out a connection and never releases it.

documents.title: Postgres FATAL: sorry, too many clients already
documents.body: When several apps and worktrees each open a pool, Postgres hits max_connections and new connections fail with FATAL 53300. Lower pool_size per app or raise max_connections.

documents.title: Ask the agent to write the migration and its rollback together
documents.body: Have the agent write the down migration in the same change and run migrate, rollback and migrate again locally before you review.

documents.title: Review agent diffs file by file
documents.body: Read the diff one file at a time and ask the agent to justify each file it touched. Unexplained files usually mean the task was not scoped clearly.

documents.title: Name the exact error string when searching for a fix
documents.body: Copy the error message exactly, including punctuation and quotes, when asking an agent or a search engine. Paraphrased errors lose the details that identify the cause.

documents.title: Keep a short project context file for agents
documents.body: A one-page file with setup commands, test commands and code conventions saves every new agent session from rediscovering the project.

documents.title: Cache dependencies in CI to cut build time
documents.body: Cache deps and _build keyed on the lockfile so CI does not recompile every dependency on each run.

documents.title: Feed the agent only the first failure from a huge test log
documents.body:
Summary: when a test run fails with hundreds of lines, do not ask the agent to summarize the whole log. Trim it to the first failure and the ten lines around it, then ask for the root cause of that one failure. Later failures are usually fallout from the first one.
